findings.reason: The protected implementation is the conventional linear reverse-stack parser for a right-associative ternary expression. Its stack, character, true_value, and false_value names expose the parser state directly; one compact block reduces each completed conditional, and the iterative traversal remains safe at the legal nesting boundary. No candidate would materially improve its correctness, complexity, clarity, or interview quality.

Scanning from right to left ensures that both branch values of a conditional have already been reduced when its condition is reached. At that point the stack suffix is question mark, true value, colon, false value in pop order, so selecting by the current T or F condition replaces the whole conditional with exactly its evaluated terminal. Repeating this reduction leaves the complete expression's single result on the stack.

Authenticated Premium source hash 13f17424e30ab6efb06e7e3a7410024eb65c64cf1ae27aa0fc9df8e095963b40, repository metadata, the solve signature, the native parseTernary method, and the modular Reference agree on a valid right-associative expression made from one-digit operands, T/F values, and ternary delimiters, with a single-character result.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064817890. App-local and native implementations reverse the same input, detect the same pending question mark, pop the same true value, colon, and false value, make the same condition-based selection, and return the same final stack value; only the required wrapper and annotation differ.

The hidden 16-, 64-, and 256-level tiers span 16x and exercise deep nested true branches. The protected source passes all 12 executions with -0.00 extra growth and a maximum observed tier ratio of 1.02x. A correct O(n^2) full-expression-rescan control passes every output but fails only scaling at +0.46 extra growth and 5.24x on the largest tier, so the unchanged benchmark is discriminating and calibrated.

The Approach accurately derives reverse processing, the pending stack layout, reduction of already-complete nested branches, right associativity, O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space, digit and Boolean terminals, and the recursion-depth benefit of the iterative structure.

The authenticated statement contains description, three explained examples, and three constraints, with no images, tables, hints, notes, or follow-up. The modular Reference preserves that order, every exact example input and output, both evaluation routes shown for examples 2 and 3, all constraint facts, and the absence of visual material; source_fidelity.json validates with no errors.

coverage: All three authenticated Premium examples appear first and in source order with exact expression and output literals; their visible Reference explanations preserve the source's selection logic and both reduction routes for examples 2 and 3.

The suite includes a valid five-character minimum and a visible 9,997-character expression, the largest complete ternary form permitted by the 10,000-character ceiling; that boundary contains 2,499 nested conditions and executes iteratively.

True and false conditions, digit and Boolean terminals, nesting in either branch, both branches nested simultaneously, right-to-left association, and repeated descent through false branches cover the material grammar semantics.

An independent forward matching-colon evaluator verified all nine visible cases and all three benchmark outputs. The protected app and immutable native implementations additionally matched it on 512 exhaustive two-level expressions and 5,000 deterministic randomized valid expression trees using seed 43920260804.

All nine correctness cases are visible samples or trials. The unchanged 16-, 64-, and 256-level workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json, and a correct quadratic control fails only their scaling verdict.
